dossier.public_summary: The dip looks flat and is the size of a 2.4 Earth-radius planet, but its depth drops by half to one-quarter from sector to sector and even from transit to transit in the same pipeline, as found by sector_depths_by_source and confirmed by transit_depths. A real planet would be steady, so the pattern positively favours a blended eclipse or variability rather than a planet on the target. Centroid is inconclusive but no close star inside one pixel needs a deep eclipse to mimic it.

reasons.why: Depth changes dramatically across sectors (2577 ppm in sector 4, 919 ppm in sector 30, 1799 ppm in sector 97)

Tool shows changes_within_a_source with per-sector depths inconsistent at p=4e-07 and single transit in sector 30 at 919 ppm 4.2 sigma shallow vs mean; real planet would be steady within a single pipeline
ML scorer trained on followed-up candidates ranks this as planet-like as only 6% of known planets, consistent with false positives that show sector-dependent depth

Observed duration 3.998 h vs 2.766 h central for TIC rad 0.5041 R_sun is long and fit requires inflated density, with near-grazing geometry; combined with depth scatter positively favours EB/contamination over a planet on-target
